broken-heart: Its nickname 'broken heart' comes from the leaves — each one is split by holes, like a heart in pieces.
alocasia: Alocasia leaves channel rain off their tips — the veins work like gutters in their native rainforests.
betel-leaf-plant-magai-paan: Maghai paan is considered the finest betel leaf in India — a tradition of growing and eating paan that's centuries old.
spider-plant-with-hanging-pot: Spider plants produce baby 'spiderettes' on long stems — each one is a ready-made clone you can pot up and gift.
vinca-rosea-sadabahar: Sadabahar means 'ever-blooming' in Hindi — the plant lives up to its name by flowering nearly every day of the year.
hanging-tomato-cherry: Cherry tomatoes ripen from the bottom of the truss upward — pick them when they detach with a gentle twist.
cherry-red-tomato: A tomato's flavour comes from a balance of sugars and acids — sun-ripened on the plant is always sweeter than picked early.
mint-plant-pudina: Pudina is a natural spreader — one plant can carpet a whole bed in a season, which is why gardeners give it its own pot.
tulsi-holy-basil: Tulsi is sacred in Indian homes — and it's also a natural mosquito repellent grown on balconies for centuries.
aloe-vera-plant: Aloe vera gel is 99% water — the remaining 1% does all the soothing work on skin.
bougainvillea-glabra: Bougainvillea's colourful 'flowers' are actually leaves — the real flowers are the tiny white centres.
curry-leaf-plant-meethi-neem: Curry leaves lose their aroma within days of picking — fresh from the plant beats any packet.
marigold-genda: Marigolds are planted alongside vegetables to repel nematodes in the soil — a living pest shield.
hibiscus-red-lal-gudhal: A hibiscus bloom lasts a single day — but a healthy plant produces new flowers daily through the season.
money-plant-golden-pothos: Golden pothos can grow in water alone indefinitely — cuttings live in bottles for years, roots and all.
